bundle.text:
# dsh-plugin-rea — one-plugin bundle
#
# Registers the REA MCP server as mcp__rea__* and launches it through the
# bundle's own shim, which reads the machine-local state written by
# `scripts/setup.mjs` and exports exactly the variables REA reads.
#
# PORTABLE BY CONSTRUCTION — no machine path appears in this file.
#   * `command` is the running Node executable (`process.execPath`), so the
#     launcher needs no PATH entry and no shim resolution by the OS.
#   * `args[0]` is computed at boot from DSH_HOME, where setup mirrors the shim.
#   * FORWARD SLASHES ONLY in the JS string literals below. A single-quoted YAML
#     scalar keeps backslashes literal, and JavaScript then eats them: '\plugins'
#     is not "\plugins" but the BEL control character, '\rea-bundle' becomes a
#     carriage return and '\bin' a backspace, so the path is silently destroyed.
#     Forward slashes are accepted on Windows and are correct on POSIX, so one
#     expression serves every platform.
#   * `path`/`require` are not in scope for a `!!js` expression (`ctx` is the
#     loader scope), hence plain string concatenation.
#   * No DSH_HOME (undefined/absent/empty) falls back to the SAME rule the shim
#     and setup.mjs use — `<home>/.dsh` — never to the bare home directory.
#     Getting this wrong is silent: setup would mirror the shim into
#     `<home>/.dsh/plugins/rea-bundle/bin/` while the row looked for it one level
#     up, so the row could never start on a machine that merely happened to have
#     DSH_HOME unset.
#   * The home fallback mirrors Node's own `os.homedir()`: USERPROFILE, then
#     HOMEDRIVE+HOMEPATH (the shape a service account gets), then HOME. An
#     expression that checked only USERPROFILE and HOME produced `/.dsh/...` —
#     the root of the current drive — for a service account, which is neither
#     where setup mirrors the shim nor a path anything can read.
#
# One row may use serverName: rea in a profile. To pin a different launch
# command on this machine, override `mcp-rea` from the profile's own
# cordis.patch.yml (id-targeted config override) — that file is never published.

- insert:
    - id: mcp-rea
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client'
      config:
        serverName: rea
        transport: stdio
        command: !!js process.execPath
        args:
          # DOUBLE-QUOTED on purpose. A bare scalar containing "? " and ": " is not
          # one scalar at all: YAML reads `? a : b` as an explicit key/value pair,
          # so js-yaml hands the loader a mapping instead of an expression node and
          # args[0] becomes an object the launcher cannot use. Quoting makes the
          # scalar unambiguous; the JS string literals inside use single quotes so
          # they cannot collide with the YAML ones.
          - !!js "(process.env.DSH_HOME && process.env.DSH_HOME.trim() !== '' ? process.env.DSH_HOME : (process.env.USERPROFILE || ((process.env.HOMEDRIVE || '') + (process.env.HOMEPATH || '')) || process.env.HOME || '') + '/.dsh') + '/plugins/rea-bundle/bin/rea-shim.mjs'"
          - mcp
        env:
          # Only meaningful when the harness itself runs on Electron; harmless
          # for a plain Node host. Explicit is better than relying on this
          # variable happening to survive the child-env scrub.
          ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE: '1'
        failOnStartupError: false

    # The Web GUI's one-shot setup guide. This row loads only the package entry
    # (index.mjs), which serves a read-only GET /dsh-plugin-rea/guide-state and
    # mounts nothing when the host has no webServer. It does not launch REA, does
    # not provision, and never runs setup for the user — the guide only reports
    # that the recorded bundle does not match the pin this package ships.
    - id: rea-guide
      name: 'dsh-plugin-rea'

**English** · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

> **Which version is this? 2.x — and `main` is it.** 2.x provisions the runtime itself (Node, the REA CLI, a
> JDK, Ghidra) and then wires the row: install the plugin, run `scripts/setup.mjs` once, restart dsh.
> **1.x** is the older configuration-only adapter — it expects `rea` on PATH and Ghidra installed by you —
> kept on the [`v1` branch](https://github.com/czcdr/dsh-plugin-rea/tree/v1) and on npm as `dsh-plugin-rea@1.0.6`.
> Full comparison: [Two lines: 1.x and 2.x](#two-lines-1x-and-2x) · upgrading: [Upgrading from 1.x](#upgrading-from-1x).

> REA **6.8.0** — this package's pin — still accepts Ghidra **12.1.x** only (12.2 is `unsupported`, and the whole
> Ghidra decompile/analysis group disappears) and the jadx bridge **0.7.1** only (0.8.0 fails on its first call with
> `Expected engine 0.7.1`, before any APK is loaded). Both gates were re-checked against 6.8.0 on 2026-10-26 and
> neither one moved. JDK **21.0.13** is out upstream, but Adoptium publishes no Windows build of it, so there is
> nothing to point at here — and it drops only three of the four eMudhra anchors. The trade-off is therefore "all
> tools green, CVE still open": Ghidra 12.1.4's CVE-2026-100504 / 100505 / 100503 / 113604 stay in the chain — **do
> not analyse untrusted samples with this environment** — and the JDK still trusts the eMudhra anchors. Evidence,
> mitigations and revisit triggers: [docs/update-review-2026-10-24.md](docs/update-review-2026-10-24.md) and
> [docs/update-review-2026-10-26.md](docs/update-review-2026-10-26.md).
>
> **Ghidra 12.2 itself works** — measured 2026-10-26: same 9 segments, same 341 procedures, byte-identical `entry`
> pseudocode as 12.1.4, through REA's own bridge. What blocks it is REA's version-equality check, not

> **You must run `node scripts/setup.mjs` yourself — once after installing, and once after every plugin
> upgrade.** Nothing runs it for you: a market install or update replaces the package and stops there.
> Since **2.0.8** a market upgrade keeps the *row* working (the mirrored launcher re-execs the new one), but it
> does **not** move the bundle to the new pins — REA and the engines stay at the versions recorded by the last
> setup run. Skip it on a first install and the row exits `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` with no tools and no message;
> skip it after an upgrade and you keep running the old REA silently (`check-updates.ps1` reports the drift).
> If you had enabled the Ghidra gate override (see §9 of the 2026-10-26 review), that setup run re-provisions the
> bundled REA and the patch goes with it — re-enable it afterwards, or accept the pinned Ghidra again.
> The full rule set is under [Updating](#updating--three-independent-things).

> **A first install and every plugin upgrade also show a one-time guide in the Web GUI.** It says whether the
> runtime is missing or behind this package's pin, shows the exact `node "<install path>/scripts/setup.mjs"`
> command for that install, and remembers the dismissal per plugin version. It is a notice only: it never runs
> setup for you and never edits the bundle. Run it once, restart dsh, and the guide stays away until the next
> plugin version.

Brings the upstream **[REA — Reverse Engineer Anything](https://github.com/morluto/rea)** MCP server into
**DeepSeek Harness** (dsh), so its tools show up in a session as `mcp__rea__*`.

A **Cordis bundle with a provisioning layer**. `package.json` declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, and that patch
inserts one row of the official MCP client plugin (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client`). The row launches
`bin/rea-shim.mjs` with the running Node executable; the shim reads the machine-local state that
`scripts/setup.mjs` wrote and starts the REA CLI it provisioned. There is no analysis code here, and the
published patch contains no machine path.

> **Third-party adapter.** This repository is not part of REA, ships none of REA's code, and is not
> maintained by REA's authors. It composes one configuration row and fetches upstream's own releases.
> Upstream: [github.com/morluto/rea](https://github.com/morluto/rea) (MIT) ·
> [docs](https://github.com/morluto/rea#what-you-can-analyze) ·
> [rea.tools](https://rea.tools/) · npm package `rea-agents`.
> REA's own problems go to its tracker; **this plugin's** problems go to
> [this repository's issues](https://github.com/czcdr/dsh-plugin-rea/issues).

**It adds exactly three things:** the tool registration under the `mcp__rea__*` names, the per-machine
engine environment (`GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR`, `JAVA_HOME`, `REA_ADB_PATH`, `REA_APKTOOL_COMMAND`,
`REA_JADX_MCP_JAR`, `REA_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE`, …) scoped to that MCP child instead of the whole harness, and
the provisioning that puts those components on disk.

readme.section: What it can and cannot do
readme.text: The analysis is upstream's; this section only restates upstream's own contract so expectations are right.

readme.section: What it can and cannot do
readme.text:
- **It cannot recover complete source code.** For native binaries upstream returns *pseudocode and
  assembly*, for Android APKs *decompiled methods*, for JEB units *pseudocode*, and for JavaScript/Electron
  *modules and their relations*. Upstream's tool contract states the pseudocode "is decompiler output, not
  original source and not text-equivalent" to another provider's output.
- Not recoverable in practice: original identifier names, types, comments, macros and template expansion,
  build scripts and assets. Optimisation (inlining, reordering), symbol stripping, obfuscation, packing and
  VM protection only make the output worse.
- Every result carries **confidence and limitations** (`observed` / `derived` / `inferred`, plus an explicit
  limitations list). Read them as evidence, never as recovered source.
- Good for: understanding behaviour, locating an implementation, interoperability and compatible
  re-implementation, security review, migration reference. To obtain actual source code, use the legitimate
  route — the upstream repository, vendor authorisation, or the vendor's own SDK.

readme.section: What it can and cannot do
readme.text: **What provisioning cannot buy you.** These are upstream host gates, not settings this plugin forgot:

readme.section: What it can and cannot do
readme.text:
| Capability | Gate |
|---|---|
| Hopper provider | macOS only |
| IDA provider | needs your own IDA and `REA_IDA_MCP_CONFIG`; REA never launches IDA |
| firmware `binwalk` / `unblob` | Linux only |
| Wakaru JS recovery, pwntools ELF/recorded-crash paths | Linux x64 only |
| pwndbg / gdb core context | Linux, macOS |
| native mitmproxy captures | Linux (`REA_MITMDUMP_COMMAND`); HAR needs no engine |
| Apple toolchain (Mach-O, plist, asset catalog, LLDB) | macOS only |
| `capture_process_scenario` | Linux/macOS PTY |
| apktool (Android resource decoding) | available only when `REA_APKTOOL_COMMAND` points at something Node can **execute directly**: upstream `execFile`s that command without a shell, and Windows cannot execute a `.bat`/`.cmd` that way (EINVAL). This bundle wires the official `apktool.bat` as upstream documents, so on Windows the launcher reports no version and the capability stays unavailable; JADX (a jar) is unaffected |

| | **2.x** — this line, `main` | **1.x** — [`v1`](https://github.com/czcdr/dsh-plugin-rea/tree/v1) |
|---|---|---|
| What it is | the adapter **plus provisioning**: it prepares Node, the REA CLI, a JDK and Ghidra, then wires the row | configuration-only adapter: one MCP row pointing at a `rea` you installed yourself |
| What you need first | nothing for the runtime — provisioning fetches what is missing (with `--reuse` it adopts an existing Ghidra/JDK instead) | Node.js on REA's engines, `npm i -g rea-agents`, and Ghidra 12.1.x for native analysis |
| First run | run `scripts/setup.mjs` (or the bootstrap) once, then restart dsh | nothing to run |
| The row launches | the running Node executable plus `<DSH_HOME>/plugins/rea-bundle/bin/rea-shim.mjs`, which reads that machine's state | `cmd.exe /c rea mcp` on Windows, `rea mcp` on macOS/Linux |
| Machine state | `<DSH_HOME>/plugins/rea-bundle/` — `bundle.json`, `vendor/`, `cache/` | your own REA and Ghidra installs |
| Install | `dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-plugin-rea` (npm `latest` ≥ 2.0.0) | `… add dsh-plugin-rea@1.0.6`, or `github:czcdr/dsh-plugin-rea#v1.0.6` |

Both lines ship the **same patch shape** — one `insert` row of `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` — and offer the
same `mcp__rea__*` surface; they differ in who prepares the runtime. Moving from 1.x to 2.x takes two
commands: see [Upgrading from 1.x](#upgrading-from-1x).

Upstream also registers itself with dsh now (`rea setup --client dsh`); that route is essentially the
1.x model maintained upstream — configuration only, your own Node/REA/Ghidra. This bundle is the
zero-dependency route. Pick one of the three, and never keep two `serverName: rea` rows at once.

**Nothing to install first.** On a bare Windows x64 machine:

```
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\rea-bundle-bootstrap.ps1 -Reuse
```

`-Reuse` adopts a Ghidra/JDK you already have; omit it to download both (about 775 MB from the official
releases, checksum-verified). Then install the plugin for your profile:

```
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-plugin-rea

readme.section: or pin this release instead of tracking npm latest:
readme.text:
Node, when you provide it instead of letting setup fetch one, must satisfy REA's engines —
`^22.23.4 || ^24.22.1 || >=26.12.1` (check with `node -v`). REA raised those floors in 6.8.0: the pinned
24.22.1 is now the *oldest* acceptable 24.x, so a 24.11–24.21 runtime that 6.7.0 accepted is rejected here.
A lower Node does not fail at install time; the MCP row fails later, which reads as silence.

readme.section: or pin this release instead of tracking npm latest:
readme.text:
Installing the plugin **first** also works, but it takes two steps. The row resolves to
`<DSH_HOME>/plugins/rea-bundle/bin/rea-shim.mjs`, and that file is created by setup — so until the first
provisioning run the row exits with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, and nothing is there to start a background
provisioning (the harness itself is unaffected: `failOnStartupError: false` is deliberate). Run
`node scripts/setup.mjs` once; from then on the shim is in place, and every later missing state is picked up
by the shim itself, which provisions in the background.

`package.json` declares `engines.dsh: ">=0.1.7-rc.2 <0.3.0-0"`, and that declaration is the answer the plugin market
reads: with it the card says **compatible**; without it the market can only say *unknown*. The range is not a guess —
it is the dsh release list this plugin is checked against, and `node scripts/host-compat.mjs` fails the build when the
two disagree:

| Host | Covered |
|---|---|
| `0.1.7-rc.2` … `0.2.1-rc.2` — every release in between, alpha and rc | yes |
| `0.3.0` and later | no — a new minor line is a host nobody updated this row for yet |

What was actually compared across that range is the row provider: `packages/mcp/mcp-client` at `dsh-v0.1.7-rc.2` and at
`dsh-v0.2.1-rc.2` exposes the same config surface the shipped row uses (`serverName`, `transport`, `command`, `args`,
`env`, `failOnStartupError`), and `dsh.bundle.patch` exists at both tags. A host outside the range can still work; it is
simply not claimed.

readme.section: A REA you already have is used as-is
readme.text:
2.x exists to supply what a machine is missing. If REA is already installed — `rea` on PATH, the 1.x setup — the row
runs **that**, exactly as the 1.x line did, and nothing is provisioned:

readme.section: A REA you already have is used as-is
readme.text:
| What the machine has | What the row runs |
|---|---|
| `rea` on PATH, at least as new as the provisioned build | your REA (`rea mcp`), with your Node and your PATH |
| `rea` on PATH but older than the provisioned build | the provisioned bundle — a stale global CLI would take the tool count backwards (6.4.0 ships 170 tools, 6.7.0 ships 207, 6.8.0 ships 229) |
| no `rea` on PATH | the provisioned bundle, provisioning itself on first use |

readme.section: A REA you already have is used as-is
readme.text:
- `REA_BUNDLE_LAUNCH=auto|system|bundle` overrides the decision (`auto` is the default); `REA_BUNDLE_SYSTEM_REA=<path>`
  names a binary that is not on PATH.
- The probe is the CLI's own `--version`, bounded at 8 s: a `.cmd` shim on Windows takes ~2.4 s to answer, so the check
  runs once per start and only when a `rea` actually exists.
- `--shim-status` prints the decision — `launch.mode`, `launch.reason`, `launch.systemRea` — and its `launch.rejected`
  list says why a candidate was skipped (`"exit 7"`, `"inside the bundle"`, `"timeout"`).
- A delegated child carries `REA_BUNDLE_DELEGATED=1`, so a wrapper that calls this shim cannot make it delegate to
  itself forever.
- **On Windows a forced kill of the shim does not reap the delegated REA.** There is no job object here: Task Manager
  or a supervisor terminating the shim leaves your `rea` running with the row's pipes (a console Ctrl+C reaches the
  whole process group and does stop it). On POSIX the child is in the same group and dies with the terminal.

The shipped row carries **no machine path**:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: mcp-rea
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client'
      config:

Three details in that row are load-bearing, and all three were bugs first:

- **The `!!js` scalar is quoted.** A bare scalar containing `? ` and `: ` is not one scalar: YAML reads it as an explicit key/value pair, so the loader receives a *mapping* where an expression belongs. Measured against the harness's own dialect (`JSON_SCHEMA` plus the `!!js` type from `app.asar`), the unquoted form made `args[0]` into `{"[object Object]": "..."}` — an object the row cannot launch with. Quoting removes the ambiguity, and the JS string literals inside then use single quotes.
- **Forward slashes, never backslashes.** A single-quoted YAML scalar keeps `\` literal, and JavaScript then consumes it: `'\plugins'` is not a path but the BEL control character, `'\rea-bundle'` becomes a carriage return and `'\bin'` a backspace — the path is destroyed silently. Forward slashes work on Windows and on POSIX.
- **The `DSH_HOME` fallback is `<home>/.dsh`, not `<home>`.** The shim, `setup.mjs` and `bootstrap.ps1` all resolve an unset `DSH_HOME` to `<home>/.dsh/...`; a fallback that stopped one level higher made the row point at a file provisioning never writes — invisible on any machine where `DSH_HOME` happens to be set.
- **The home fallback mirrors `os.homedir()`: `USERPROFILE`,

`npm run bundle:audit` enforces the first three: it evaluates this exact expression with `DSH_HOME` unset, empty and set, and rejects a bare scalar that YAML would read as a mapping.

`ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE` only matters if the harness itself runs on Electron; it is harmless for a plain Node host, and stating it explicitly beats relying on it surviving the child-env scrub.

`command` is the running Node executable and `args[0]` is computed from `DSH_HOME`, so the same patch works
on Windows, macOS and Linux without a PATH entry. Everything machine-specific lives in
`<DSH_HOME>/plugins/rea-bundle/bundle.json`, written by setup and readable with:

```
node bin/rea-shim.mjs --shim-status      # resolved paths, versions, verification state
node bin/rea-shim.mjs --shim-print-env   # the environment the MCP child will see
```

Both commands answer with the same bundle whether you run them from the plugin directory (the checkout copy)
or from `<DSH_HOME>/plugins/rea-bundle` (the mirrored copy): the checkout resolves the location by the same
rule setup uses, while the mirror uses its own position — it cannot rely on `DSH_HOME`, which the harness
strips from an MCP child's environment.

Setting `REA_BUNDLE_AUTO_PROVISION=0` disables the first-run background provisioning.

To pin a different launch command on this machine (for example your own globally installed `rea`), override
the row from the profile's own `cordis.patch.yml` — that file is machine-local and never published. Only one
row may use `serverName: rea` in a profile.

A patch replaces the row's `config` **wholesale** — it does not deep-merge — so a partial override such as
`config: {env: {...}}` also deletes `command`, `args` and `serverName`, and the row stops starting. Supply the
complete config, or use `REA_BUNDLE_LAUNCH=system` (above), which needs no patch at all.

Ghidra and the JDK are not read from your environment at launch: `setup.mjs` records their absolute paths in
`bundle.json` and the shim exports `GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR` / `JAVA_HOME` from that record — which is why a
non-standard install location works without touching the row. To adopt an existing install, point
`GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR` / `JAVA_HOME` at it and run `node scripts/setup.mjs --reuse`: the manifest's probe checks
the candidate and falls back to a download when it does not match, so a wrong path is reported during setup
instead of failing later inside a tool call.

Upstream REA 6.5.0 can register itself with DSH:

```
rea setup --client dsh
```

That writes a row with `id: rea-mcp` and `serverName: rea` into `<DSH_HOME>/cordis.patch.yml`. This
bundle's row is `id: mcp-rea` with the same `serverName`, and DSH rejects the later of two entries
that share a server name — so which REA row survives depends on load order. **Use one, not both.**

Which one? Upstream's is the configuration-only route: it expects Node on REA's engines,
`rea-agents` reachable, and a Ghidra/JDK you provisioned yourself. This bundle is the
zero-dependency route: it fetches Node, REA, JDK and Ghidra on first run. The patch shape and the
`mcp__rea__*` surface are the same either way.

The shim reports the conflict on startup — `setup.mjs` records the DSH home it ran under in
`mirror.json`, and the mirrored copy reads that when the harness has stripped `DSH_*` from its
environment; `node bin/rea-shim.mjs --shim-status` lists it under `duplicateRegistration`.

Ask for a `mcp__rea__*` call — `binary_session` reports the engine checks
(`configuration` / `installation` / `headless` / `native_decompiler` / `java`), all of which should be
`ok: true`. Then `open_binary` a PE, `binary_overview`, and `procedure_pseudo_code`.

Provisioning itself ends with three checks: `rea doctor --json` (reported, with unmet checks named), a
**Ghidra smoke import** that runs `rea analyze` on the JDK's own `bin/java` and fails the run when it
cannot import (`--skip-smoke` omits it), and the exact shim launch the MCP row will use. The smoke step
exists because `doctor` validates paths, versions and which Java would be chosen — it never imports a
binary, so a broken bridge or a mismatched native addon used to surface only as an MCP timeout.

**The first analysis of each new target is slow.** Measured here: 36 s for a small PE, 64 s for a 6 MB
DLL — every import starts a JVM and runs Ghidra's default auto-analysis. If the first
`open_binary` → `list_segments` on a large file times out, that is this cost and not a broken engine:
call it again and the open target answers immediately, because it keeps its ephemeral project.

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| REA (`rea-agents`) | **6.8.0** (229 tools) |
| DeepSeek Harness | desktop runtime **0.2.0-rc.2**, with its bundled dsh CLI 0.1.7-rc.2 |
| `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` (row provider) | bundled by the harness |
| Ghidra | 12.1.4 |
| JDK | Temurin 21 (provisioned) / Amazon Corretto 25.0.5 (adopted by the host) |
| Node.js | **24.22.1** adopted (REA engines: `^22.23.4 \|\| ^24.22.1 \|\| >=26.12.1`; ABI 137) |
| Host | Windows 11 x64 (build 26200) |

Exercised live: a clean `setup.mjs --reuse` run reached `setup complete`; an MCP `initialize` handshake
**through the shim with no `rea` on PATH** answered `serverInfo {name: rea, version: 6.8.0}`; and the whole
chain ran under the real desktop host — its own Electron binary launched
`<DSH_HOME>/plugins/rea-bundle/bin/rea-shim.mjs mcp`, the shim started the **vendored** REA, and a live tool
call reported `path_source: environment` for a path only that machine's `bundle.json` knows.

Not exercised end to end here, and therefore not claimed: the ~775 MB JDK + Ghidra download branch (planned
by `--dry-run`, but this machine adopted its existing installs with `--reuse`), and first runs on
macOS/Linux.

On 2026-10-23 the same chain was re-verified after the host Node moved to **24.22.1**: the vendored
`rea-windows-x64.node` and both `conpty` addons loaded under ABI 137; `binary_overview` on `conpty.node`
reported 10 segments / 1178 procedures / 618 strings; `procedure_pseudo_code` returned real decompiled
output; and `java -version` from the vendored JDK answered `21.0.12.1`. The one thing that did **not**
work on the first try was the first `list_segments` — it timed out at 64 s of cold Ghidra analysis, which
is what the smoke step and the note above are for.

On 2026-10-26 the pin moved to **REA 6.8.0** and the chain was re-verified on the same machine: `setup.mjs
--reuse` reported `probe cli=6.8.0 tools=229` and its Ghidra smoke imported `java.exe` in 26 s; an independent
MCP handshake over stdio answered `serverInfo {name: rea, version: 6.8.0}` with **229 tools / 6 prompts** on
protocol `2024-11-05`; apktool still answers `3.0.3`, `adb` still reports 37.0.1 (1.0.41), and the jadx jar on
disk still hashes to `6e5eacf5…` — the value REA 6.8.0 requires. Executing 6.8.0's own release policy gave
`12.1.4 → verified`, `12.1.5 → compatible`, `12.2 → unsupported`, so Ghidra stays where it was.

- REA exposes 229 tools at 6.8.0, so every session's tool list grows.

> **Two standing rules — for this release and for every later 2.x release.**
>
> `setup.mjs` reconciles the **bundle**, never the **plugin**: it reads the manifest of the plugin that is

> only through the market (or `npm i -g dsh-plugin-rea@<version>` / a `file:` reinstall); running setup more
> often never substitutes for that.
>

> `setup.mjs` — and one after every upgrade — is yours to run, from the plugin directory.

>    running old code with **no symptom at all**. Since **2.0.8** the mirror compares itself with the launcher
>    recorded in `mirror.json` and re-execs the plugin's copy when the two differ (one hop, guarded by

Update it where you installed it. Updating **to 2.0.5 or later** is routine; updating an installed 2.0.1–2.0.4
*through the in-app market* failed with this, three times on a healthy profile:

> dsh-plugin-rea 更新后缺少入口文件（package.json 的 main/exports 指向的文件不存在），且未能验证恢复原版本文件

That message is not about a broken tarball. On every update the market asks whether the new build's
`package.json` points at an entry file that exists (`hasLoadableEntry` in `dshmarket`), and rolls the build back
when the answer is false. A bundle may legitimately own no entry — but only if a package it *mounts* has one, and
the package this bundle mounts (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client`) ships inside the harness build rather than in
`node_modules`, so every location that test probes comes back empty. The 1.x and 2.0.x manifests also declared
no `main` at all, so the answer was false even though the profile was working; the rollback was then reported as
unverifiable for the same reason. Nothing in the profile was actually damaged — the update simply did not apply.

2.0.5 declares `main: ./index.mjs`. That file is a real, deliberately empty Cordis plugin: it registers nothing,
spawns nothing, touches no state — the working row is still inserted by `cordis.patch.yml` — and it exists so the
question "can this package load?" has an honest answer, and so `import 'dsh-plugin-rea'` resolves. On an older
version, update to `>=2.0.5`; if the market refuses before that version exists, install `dsh-plugin-rea@2.0.5`
(Desktop: through the plugin manager) instead of updating in place.

Install 2.x, then run provisioning **once** before restarting dsh:

```
node scripts/setup.mjs          # or: powershell -File scripts\rea-bundle-bootstrap.ps1 -Reuse
```

Why it matters: the 1.x row launched `rea mcp` from PATH, while the 2.x row launches
`<DSH_HOME>/plugins/rea-bundle/bin/rea-shim.mjs` — a file only `setup.mjs` creates. Upgrade and restart
without provisioning and that row exits with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`: the harness stays up
(`failOnStartupError: false` is deliberate), but the `mcp__rea__*` tools are gone and you get **no
remediation message**, because the shim that prints one does not exist yet. After the setup run they are
back on the next start.

- **This plugin** never updates itself. Installed from a market? Update it there. Installed from a `file:`
  checkout? Overwrite the directory and reinstall.
- **The row runs a COPY of this plugin's launcher.** `<DSH_HOME>/plugins/rea-bundle/bin/rea-shim.mjs` is a mirror

  again. From **2.0.8** the mirror notices that the installed plugin ships a different launcher and re-execs it
  (one hop, guarded by `REA_BUNDLE_SHIM_REEXEC`), so upgrades carry. On an older version the mirror stays behind
  silently; `--shim-status` now reports `mirror.stale`, and `check-updates.ps1` says to re-run setup. If you are
  upgrading from 2.0.0–2.0.7, run `node scripts/setup.mjs` once after the upgrade.
- **The mirrored `scripts/setup.mjs` is a copy too.** A market upgrade replaces the package but not that copy,

  when the bundle was created — not the one you just installed. From **2.0.9** both the shim and setup strip a
  UTF-8 BOM from `mirror.json` / `bundle.json` (a BOM-ed recor

forwards to it on Windows (PowerShell 5.1, then `pwsh`); on macOS/Linux it prints why the script cannot
answer there and names the two portable commands instead — `node bin/rea-shim.mjs --shim-status` and
`node scripts/setup.mjs --dry-run` — exiting non-zero rather than reporting a green it did not earn.

```

把上游 **[REA — Reverse Engineer Anything](https://github.com/morluto/rea)** 的 MCP 服务接入
**DeepSeek Harness**（dsh），让它的工具在会话里以 `mcp__rea__*` 出现。

一个**带供给层的 Cordis bundle**。`package.json` 声明 `dsh.bundle.patch`，该 patch 插入一行官方 MCP 客户端
插件（`@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client`）。这一行用当前运行的 Node 可执行文件启动 `bin/rea-shim.mjs`，由 shim
读取 `scripts/setup.mjs` 写下的本机状态，再拉起它供给的 REA CLI。这里没有任何分析代码，且**发布出去的
patch 里不含任何机器路径**。

> **第三方适配。** 本仓库不属于 REA，不携带 REA 的任何代码，也不由 REA 作者维护；它只组装一行配置，
> 并从上游官方源拉取上游自己的发布物。
> 上游：[github.com/morluto/rea](https://github.com/morluto/rea)（MIT）·
> [中文文档](https://github.com/morluto/rea/blob/main/README_zh.md#可以分析什么) ·
> [rea.tools](https://rea.tools/) · npm 包 `rea-agents`。
> REA 自身的问题请提给上游；**本插件**的问题提到
> [本仓库 issues](https://github.com/czcdr/dsh-plugin-rea/issues)。

**它只做三件事**：注册 `mcp__rea__*` 这批工具名；把每台机器各自的引擎环境
（`GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR`、`JAVA_HOME`、`REA_ADB_PATH`、`REA_APKTOOL_COMMAND`、`REA_JADX_MCP_JAR`、
`REA_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE` 等）限定在那一个 MCP 子进程上、而不是整个 harness；以及把这些组件装到盘上。

分析能力属上游，本节只是复述上游自己的契约，避免预期错位。

- **它无法还原完整源码。** 原生二进制上游给的是*伪代码与汇编*，APK 是*反编译方法*，JEB 单元是*伪代码*，
  JavaScript/Electron 是*模块及其关系*。上游的工具契约明确写着伪代码"是反编译器输出，不是原始源码，
  也不与另一 provider 的输出文本等价"。
- 实际上拿不回来的：原始标识符名、类型、注释、宏与模板展开、构建脚本与资源。优化（内联、重排）、
  符号剥离、混淆、加壳、VM 保护只会让输出更差。
- 每个结果都带**置信度与限制**（`observed` / `derived` / `inferred`，外加一份明确的 limitations 列表）。
  请当证据读，别当还原出来的源码。
- 适合：理解行为、定位实现、互操作与兼容重写、安全审阅、迁移参考。要拿真正的源码，走正规渠道 ——
  上游仓库、厂商授权，或厂商自己的 SDK。

**供给解决不了的部分。** 这些是上游的宿主门槛，不是本插件漏配了什么：

| 能力 | 门槛 |
|---|---|
| Hopper provider | 仅 macOS |
| IDA provider | 需要你自己的 IDA 与 `REA_IDA_MCP_CONFIG`；REA 从不启动 IDA |
| 固件 `binwalk` / `unblob` | 仅 Linux |
| Wakaru JS 还原、pwntools 的 ELF/宕机转储路径 | 仅 Linux x64 |

| 原生 mitmproxy 抓包 | 仅 Linux（`REA_MITMDUMP_COMMAND`）；HAR 不需要引擎 |
| 苹果工具链（Mach-O、plist、资源目录、LLDB） | 仅 macOS |
| `capture_process_scenario` | 仅 Linux/macOS 的 PTY |
| apktool（Android 资源解码） | 仅当 `REA_APKTOOL_COMMAND` 指向 Node 能**直接执行**的文件时才可用：上游用 `execFile` 不加 shell 直接起这个命令，而 Windows 上 Node 无法直接执行 `.bat`/`.cmd`（EINVAL）。本包按上游文档接的是官方 `apktool.bat`，所以在 Windows 上它拿不到版本、该能力不可用；JADX 走 jar，不受影响 |

readme.section: 或钉住这个版本，而不是跟着 npm latest 走：
readme.text:
如果 Node 由你自备（而不是让 setup 去取），它必须满足 REA 的 engines：
`^22.23.4 || ^24.22.1 || >=26.12.1`（用 `node -v` 核对）。REA 在 6.8.0 抬了这条下限：钉住的 24.22.1
现在是 24 线**最低**可接受版本，6.7.0 能吃下的 24.11–24.21 在这里会被拒。版本偏低不会在安装时失败，
而是到 MCP 行启动时才失败 —— 表现就是"没有反应"。

readme.section: 或钉住这个版本，而不是跟着 npm latest 走：
readme.text:
反过来**先装插件**也可以，但要分两步：发布的行指向 `<DSH_HOME>/plugins/rea-bundle/bin/rea-shim.mjs`，
而那个文件**只有 setup 会创建**——所以在第一次供给之前，该行会以 `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` 退出，也就没有
任何东西能去启动后台供给（harness 本身不受影响：`failOnStartupError: false` 是刻意的）。先手动跑一次
`node scripts/setup.mjs`；此后 shim 就位，之后每一次「状态缺失」都由它自己发现并在后台补供给。

readme.section: 支持哪些 DSH 版本
readme.text:
`package.json` 里声明了 `engines.dsh: ">=0.1.7-rc.2 <0.3.0-0"`，这就是插件市场读的那句话：有它，卡片显示
**兼容**；没有它，市场只能说*未声明*。这个范围不是猜的——它对应本插件实际核对过的 dsh 发布列表，
`node scripts/host-compat.mjs` 会在两者不一致时让构建失败：

| 宿主版本 | 是否覆盖 |
|---|---|
| `0.1.7-rc.2` … `0.2.1-rc.2`（中间的 alpha 与 rc 全部在内） | 是 |
| `0.3.0` 及以后 | 否 —— 新的小版本线是还没为它核对过这一行的宿主 |

readme.section: 支持哪些 DSH 版本
readme.text:
真正被比对过的是「行提供方」：`packages/mcp/mcp-client` 在 `dsh-v0.1.7-rc.2` 与 `dsh-v0.2.1-rc.2` 两个 tag 上，
暴露的配置面与发布的行完全一致（`serverName`、`transport`、`command`、`args`、`env`、`failOnStartupError`），
并且两个 tag 都有 `dsh.bundle.patch`。范围之外的宿主可能照样能用，只是没有替它声明。

readme.section: 机器上已有 REA 就直接用它
readme.text:
2.x 存在的意义是补上机器缺的东西。如果 REA 已经装好——`rea` 在 PATH 上，也就是 1.x 的形态——这一行就**直接跑它**，
和 1.x 一模一样，不再做任何供给：

| 机器上的情况 | 这一行跑什么 |
|---|---|
| `rea` 在 PATH 上，且不比供给的版本旧 | 你自己那份（`rea mcp`），用你的 Node 和你的 PATH |
| `rea` 在 PATH 上，但比供给的版本旧 | 供给出来的 bundle —— 旧的全局 CLI 会把工具数往回退（6.4.0 是 170 个，6.7.0 是 207 个，6.8.0 是 229 个） |
| PATH 上没有 `rea` | 供给出来的 bundle，首次使用时自行供给 |

readme.section: 机器上已有 REA 就直接用它
readme.text:
- `REA_BUNDLE_LAUNCH=auto|system|bundle` 覆盖这个判断（默认 `auto`）；`REA_BUNDLE_SYSTEM_REA=<path>` 用来点名一个
  不在 PATH 上的可执行文件。
- 探测用的是 CLI 自己的 `--version`，上限 8 秒：Windows 上的 `.cmd` 垫片要 ~2.4 秒才答得出来，所以这个检查每次启动
  只做一次，而且只在真的存在 `rea` 时才做。
- `--shim-status` 会把判断结果打出来 —— `launch.mode`、`launch.reason`、`launch.systemRea`，`launch.rejected` 里
  写的是每个候选被跳过的原因（`"exit 7"`、`"inside the bundle"`、`"timeout"`）。
- 被委派的子进程带着 `REA_BUNDLE_DELEGATED=1`，所以一个调用本 shim 的 wrapper 不会让它无限委派给自己。
- **Windows 上强制结束 shim 不会带走被委派的 REA**：这里没有 job object，任务管理器或 supervisor 终止 shim 时，
  你自己的 `rea` 会继续占着这一行的管道（控制台 Ctrl+C 会发给整个进程组，那种情况下会一起停）。POSIX 上子进程
  在同一进程组，随终端一起退出。

发布的那一行**不含任何机器路径**：

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: mcp-rea
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client'
      config:

这一行里有四个"承重"细节，而且**都先以 bug 的形式出现过**：

- **`!!js` 标量必须加引号。** 裸标量里同时出现 `? ` 和 `: ` 时，它就不是一个标量了：YAML 会把它读成显式键值对，于是 loader 拿到的是一个 **mapping** 而不是表达式节点。用 harness 自己的方言实测（`JSON_SCHEMA` + `app.asar` 里的 `!!js` 类型），不加引号时 `args[0]` 变成 `{"[object Object]": "..."}` —— 一个行根本无法用来启动的对象。加引号消除歧义，内部的 JS 字符串改用单引号。
- **必须用正斜杠，不能用反斜杠。** YAML 单引号标量会保留 `\` 字面量，接着 JavaScript 会把它吃掉：`'\plugins'` 不是路径而是 BEL 控制字符，`'\rea-bundle'` 变成回车、`'\bin'` 变成退格 —— 路径被静默摧毁。正斜杠在 Windows 与 POSIX 上都成立。
- **`DSH_HOME` 的兜底是 `<home>/.dsh`，不是 `<home>`。** shim、`setup.mjs`、`bootstrap.ps1` 三者都把未设置的 `DSH_HOME` 解析到 `<home>/.dsh/...`；兜底少这一层，行就会指向供给永远不会写的位置 —— 而在 `DSH_HOME` 恰好被设置的机器上，这个错误完全不可见。
- **主目录兜底与 `os.homedir()` 同序：`USERPROFILE` → `HOMEDRIVE`+`HOMEPATH` → `HOME`。** 中间那一对是
  Windows 服务账户拿到的形态（没有 `USERPROFILE`）；跳过它，表达式会给这类账户算出 `/.dsh/...` —— 当前盘的根，
  而它们恰好读不到那个路径。只有四者全空（连主目录都没有的容器账户）才会落到 `/.dsh/...`，而
  `failOnStartupError: false` 会让它保持安静，症状只有「没有 `mcp__rea__*` 工具」。这类账户请显式设置 `DSH_HOME`。
- **`!!js` 表达式里没有 `path`/`require`**：`ctx` 是 loader 作用域，所以 DSH_HOME 的兜底写成纯字符串拼接。

`npm run bundle:audit` 会把前三条钉住：它用「`DSH_HOME` 未设 / 为空 / 已设」三种情形求值这个表达式，并拒绝会被 YAML 读成 mapping 的裸标量。

`ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE` 只在 harness 本身跑在 Electron 上时才有意义；对纯 Node 宿主无害，而显式写出来胜过依赖它恰好能在子进程环境清洗中存活。

`command` 是当前运行的 Node 可执行文件，`args[0]` 由 `DSH_HOME` 在启动时算出，所以同一份 patch 在
Windows、macOS、Linux 上都成立，且不依赖 PATH 上的 `rea`。所有机器相关的真相都放在
`<DSH_HOME>/plugins/rea-bundle/bundle.json`，由 setup 写入，可随时查看：

```
node bin/rea-shim.mjs --shim-status      # 解析到的路径、版本、校验状态
node bin/rea-shim.mjs --shim-print-env   # MCP 子进程将看到的环境变量
```

这两个命令在**插件目录**（checkout 副本）或 `<DSH_HOME>/plugins/rea-bundle`（镜像副本）里跑都给出同一
答案：checkout 副本按与 setup 相同的规则解析供给位置，镜像副本用自身位置（因为 MCP 子进程的环境里
`DSH_*` 会被剥掉，它不能依赖 `DSH_HOME`）。

设 `REA_BUNDLE_AUTO_PROVISION=0` 可关掉首次运行的后台自动供给。

想在本机把这一行改成别的启动命令（例如用你自己全局装的 `rea`），从 profile 自己的
`cordis.patch.yml` 按 id 覆盖即可 —— 那个文件是机器本地的，永不发布。一个 profile 里只允许一行使用
`serverName: rea`。

覆盖是**整块替换** `config`（不做深合并）：只写 `config: {env: …}` 会把 `command`、`args`、`serverName`
一起删掉，这一行就起不来了。要么写完整的 config，要么改用 `REA_BUNDLE_LAUNCH=system`（见上），它不需要改 patch。

Ghidra 和 JDK **不是启动时从环境里读的**：`setup.mjs` 把它们的绝对路径记进 `bundle.json`，shim 再从那份
记录导出 `GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR` / `JAVA_HOME` —— 所以装在非标准路径也能用，不必动这一行。要采纳现成的安装，
把 `GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR` / `JAVA_HOME` 指向它并跑 `node scripts/setup.mjs --reuse`：manifest 里的探针会验证
候选，不符合就回落到下载，**路径写错会在供给时就报出来**，而不是等到某次工具调用里才失效。

readme.section: 只保留一条 REA 注册
readme.text:
上游 REA 6.5.0 起可以自己注册进 DSH：

```
rea setup --client dsh
```

它会把一行 `id: rea-mcp`、`serverName: rea` 写进 `<DSH_HOME>/cordis.patch.yml`。本包的行是
`id: mcp-rea`、同样 `serverName: rea`，而 DSH 对同名条目只保留一个：后加载的那行会以
duplicate server name 报错并加载失败，最终留下哪一行取决于加载顺序。**二选一，不要同时用。**

选哪个？上游那条是纯配置路线：需要 Node 满足 REA engines、`rea-agents` 可达，Ghidra/JDK 由你
自己准备。本包是零依赖路线：首次运行自动取 Node、REA、JDK、Ghidra。两者的 patch 形态与
`mcp__rea__*` 工具面相同。

readme.section: 只保留一条 REA 注册
readme.text:
shim 会在启动时提示冲突 —— `setup.mjs` 会把运行时的 DSH home 记进 `mirror.json`，镜像副本在 harness 抹掉
`DSH_*` 之后就用这条记录去找那份文件；`node bin/rea-shim.mjs --shim-status` 会把冲突列在 `duplicateRegistration` 下。

随便发一个 `mcp__rea__*` 调用 —— `binary_session` 会报引擎各项检查
（`configuration` / `installation` / `headless` / `native_decompiler` / `java`），应当全为 `ok: true`。
然后 `open_binary` 一个 PE、`binary_overview`、`procedure_pseudo_code`。

供给本身结束时跑三道检查：`rea doctor --json`（如实报告，并点名未满足项）、一次 **Ghidra 冒烟导入**
（用 JDK 自带的 `bin/java` 跑 `rea analyze`，导不进就判本次供给失败；`--skip-smoke` 可关），以及
**与 MCP 行完全相同的 shim 启动**。之所以要冒烟：`doctor` 只校验路径、版本与会用哪个 Java，**从不导入
二进制**，桥接或 native addon 坏了，过去只能在第一次 MCP 调用超时时才撞见。

**每个新目标的第一次分析都很慢。** 本机实测：小 PE 36 s，6 MB 的 DLL 64 s —— 每次导入都要起 JVM 并跑
Ghidra 的默认自动分析。如果大文件的第一次 `open_binary` → `list_segments` 超时，那是这个成本、不是引擎坏了：
再调一次，已打开的目标会立刻返回（它保留着自己的临时项目）。

作者机器，2026-10-13 / 14 / 16 / 19 / 23 / 26：

| 组件 | 版本 |
|---|---|
| REA（`rea-agents`） | **6.8.0**（229 个工具） |
| DeepSeek Harness | desktop runtime **0.2.0-rc.2**，内含 dsh CLI 0.1.7-rc.2 |
| `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client`（行 provider） | 随 harness 打包 |
| Ghidra | 12.1.4 |
| JDK | Temurin 21（供给）/ Amazon Corretto 25.0.5（宿主复用） |
| Node.js | **24.22.1**（复用；REA engines：`^22.23.4 \|\| ^24.22.1 \|\| >=26.12.1`，ABI 137） |
| 宿主 | Windows 11 x64（build 26200） |

实测跑过：一次干净的 `setup.mjs --reuse` 走到 `setup complete`；一次**不经 PATH 上的 `rea`、完全经由
shim** 的 MCP `initialize` 握手返回 `serverInfo {name: rea, version: 6.8.0}`；以及**真实桌面宿主下的完整链路** ——
宿主自己的 Electron 二进制启动 `<DSH_HOME>/plugins/rea-bundle/bin/rea-shim.mjs mcp`，shim 拉起 **bundle 内置**
的 REA，随后一次真实工具调用报出 `path_source: environment`，而那个路径只有该机的 `bundle.json` 知道。

本机**没有**端到端跑过、因此不做承诺的：约 775 MB 的 JDK + Ghidra 下载分支（`--dry-run` 有计划，本机用
`--reuse` 复用了已有安装），以及 macOS/Linux 的首次运行。

2026-10-23 宿主 Node 换到 **24.22.1** 后，同一条链路重验过：vendor 里的 `rea-windows-x64.node` 与两个
`conpty` addon 在 ABI 137 下加载成功；`conpty.node` 的 `binary_overview` 报出 10 个段 / 1178 个函数 /
618 个字符串；`procedure_pseudo_code` 返回了真实反编译结果；vendor 里的 JDK `java -version` 回 `21.0.12.1`。
唯一**第一次没成**的是 `list_segments`：它撞上 Ghidra 冷分析的 64 s 而超时 —— 这正是上面冒烟步与那条说明的由来。

2026-10-26 钉子换到 **REA 6.8.0** 后，同一条链路重验过：`setup.mjs --reuse` 报 `probe cli=6.8.0 tools=229`，
末尾的 Ghidra 冒烟用 26 s 导入 `java.exe`；另起一次独立的 stdio MCP 握手回 `serverInfo {name: rea, version:
6.8.0}`，协议 `2024-11-05`，**229 个工具 / 6 个 prompt**；apktool 仍答 `3.0.3`，`adb` 仍报 37.0.1 (1.0.41)，
盘上的 jadx jar 仍是 `6e5eacf5…` —— 正是 6.8.0 要求的那个值。把 6.8.0 自己的发布策略加载执行，得到
`12.1.4 → verified`、`12.1.5 → compatible`、`12.2 → unsupported`，所以 Ghidra 原地不动。

- REA 在 6.8.0 有 229 个工具，每个会话的工具列表都会变长。
- 校验和对得起良心：厂商发布了的就固定并验证；没发布的（jadx-headless-mcp、apktool 包装脚本、
  Android platform-tools、滚动的 `latest` 地址）则**实测一次并记录**，之后若漂移是**报告**而不是默默接受。
  `bundle.json` 的 `unverifiedChecksums` 会列出处于该状态的组件。
- 某些网络下很慢（这里实测 GitHub release CDN 只有 0.35–0.54 MiB/s，光 Ghidra 就要 25–45 分钟）。
  下载是**可续传**的：两条路线都按盘上已有的字节发 Range 继续；若 `.part` 恰好已经完整，会校验后直接收下
  而不是重下。
- **代理**：Node 的全局 `fetch` 不读系统代理，而 .NET/PowerShell 会读。在开着 WinINET 代理的机器上，
  同一个地址 `Invoke-WebRequest` 通、Node 却 `ECONNRESET`/超时。setup 自己解析代理
  （环境变量优先，Windows 上回退读注册表）并用 CONNECT 隧道，`NO_PROXY` 也照常生效。
- REA 的部分工具会启动进程、写文件、访问网络 —— DSH 的权限策略照常适用。只分析你有权检视的样本。
- MCP 子进程与它拉起的引擎都是以**你的身份**运行的普通进程。DSH 的工具审批管的是模型发起的调用，
  管不到这个子进程自己去读、写或发送什么；请把插件当作你安装的第三方代码来对待。
- Linux 上，上游的进程归属检查依赖 PATH 上**兼容 procps 的 `ps`**；Ghidra/JADX 与固件工具会用到它。
  极简镜像里缺它只会让这些工具失败，不影响整体安装。
- `scripts/setup.mjs` 为 REA CLI 跑的是带 `--ignore-scripts` 的 `npm install`：官方 tarball 不带
  `node_modules`，必须解析依赖闭包；而供给过程中**刻意跳过包的 lifecycle 脚本**。这一步也是**唯一**用不上
  本插件自己的路由/代理回退的环节 —— npm 只从环境读 `HTTPS_PROXY`/`HTTP_PROXY` 与

  `NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY=https://registry.npmmirror.com`）。带 `--offline` 时这一步会被**直接拒绝**，
  而不是悄悄联网。

readme.section: 更新 —— 三件互相独立的事
readme.text:
> **两条长期规则 —— 本版如此，以后每个 2.x 版本都如此。**
>
> `setup.mjs` 只对齐 **bundle**，不更新**插件包**：它读的是「当前已安装插件」的 manifest。装着 2.0.9 时跑 setup
> 仍旧供给 6.5.0，哪怕已经有更新的一版发布。插件包只能从市场（或 `npm i -g dsh-plugin-rea@<版本>` / `file:` 重装）换，
> **多跑几次 setup 也替代不了那一步**。
>
> **而且没有人会替你跑它。** 市场里的安装/更新只替换包，然后到此为止；第一次的 `setup.mjs`，以及之后每次升级后的
> 那一次，都要你自己从插件目录跑。
>
> 1. **行执行的是本插件启动器的「镜像副本」**：`<DSH_HOME>/plugins/rea-bundle/bin/rea-shim.mjs` 由 setup 复制，
>    市场升级只换包、不换它，所以副本可能一直跑旧代码而**完全没有症状**。从 **2.0.8** 起，副本会与 `mirror.json`
>    记录的启动器比对，不同就一跳转发执行插件里的那份（带 `REA_BUNDLE_SHIM_REEXEC` 守卫）。**2.0.0–2.0.7 的镜像
>    做不到**，所以从它们升级仍需跑一次 `node scripts/setup.mjs`。`--shim-status` 会报 `mirror.stale`，
>    `check-updates.ps1` 会提示重跑。
> 2. **镜像的 `scripts/setup.mjs` 同样是副本，而且它自己不会自愈**：从 bundle 根目录跑它，跑的是建 bundle 那一版
>    的 setup，不是你刚装的这一版。要从**插件目录**跑一次来刷新这份副本。从 **2.0.9** 起，它会像 shim 一样剥掉
>    `mirror.json` / `bundle.json` 的 UTF-8 BOM —— 带 BOM 的记录以前在 setup 眼里等于「没有记录」，会把上一版
>    manifest 又镜一遍。

在哪儿装的就在哪儿更新。更新到 **2.0.5 及以上**是常规操作；而把已装的 2.0.1–2.0.4 通过应用内市场**更新到
2.0.5**，在健康的 profile 上连续失败了三次：

> dsh-plugin-rea 更新后缺少入口文件（package.json 的 main/exports 指向的文件不存在），且未能验证恢复原版本文件

这条消息与 tarball 是否完整无关。市场在每次更新时都会问一句：新构建的 `package.json` 是否指向一个真实存在的
入口文件（`dshmarket` 里的 `hasLoadableEntry`）；答案是「否」，就把这次更新判为坏构建并回滚。bundle 本来允许
自己没有入口 —— 前提是它**挂载**的某个包有入口；而本包挂载的 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` 属于 harness 自身
构建，不在 `node_modules` 里，于是这项检查要看的每个位置都是空的。1.x 与 2.0.x 的清单又根本没有声明 `main`，
所以答案必然是「否」，哪怕 profile 一直是好的；紧接着的回滚也因此被报成「无法验证」。实际上 profile 没有被
破坏，只是这次更新没有生效。

2.0.5 声明了 `main: ./index.mjs`。那是一个真实存在、刻意留空的 Cordis 插件：不注册任何行、不启动任何进程、
不碰任何状态（真正起作用的行仍由 `cordis.patch.yml` 插入），它的作用只是让「这个包能不能加载」有一个诚实的
答案，并让 `import 'dsh-plugin-rea'` 能解析。还停在旧版本时，更新到 `>=2.0.5` 即可；若市场在 2.0.5 之前就拒绝，
就直接安装 `dsh-plugin-rea@2.0.5`（桌面端：在插件管理器里装），不要原地更新。

装上 2.x 后，**先跑一次供给**，再重启 dsh：

```
node scripts/setup.mjs          # 或：powershell -File scripts\rea-bundle-bootstrap.ps1 -Reuse
```

为什么必须先跑：1.x 的行从 PATH 上启动 `rea mcp`，而 2.x 的行启动
`<DSH_HOME>/plugins/rea-bundle/bin/rea-shim.mjs` —— 那个文件**只有 `setup.mjs` 会创建**。升级后直接重启，
该行会以 `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` 退出：harness 本身照常（`failOnStartupError: false` 是刻意的），但
`mcp__rea__*` 工具会消失，而且**不会有任何修复提示** —— 会打提示的 shim 本身还不存在。跑完 setup 再启动，
工具就回来了。

- **本插件**从不自更新。从市场装的就在市场更新；从 `file:` 检出的就覆盖目录重装。
- **行跑的是本插件启动器的「镜像副本」**：`<DSH_HOME>/plugins/rea-bundle/bin/rea-shim.mjs` 是 setup 复制过去的，
  所以市场升级只换包、不换行执行的那个文件 —— 直到再跑一次 setup。从 **2.0.8** 起，镜像会发现自己落后于已安装的
  插件，并转发执行插件里的那一份（一跳，带 `REA_BUNDLE_SHIM_REEXEC` 守卫），升级因此能生效。更早的版本里镜像会
  静默地停在旧代码；`--shim-status` 现在会报 `mirror.stale`，`check-updates.ps1` 也会提示重跑 setup。**从
  2.0.0–2.0.7 升级的话，升级后跑一次 `node scripts/setup.mjs`。**
- **镜像的 `scripts/setup.mjs` 同样是副本。** 市场升级只换包、不换它，所以照着提示去跑
  `<DSH_HOME>/plugins/rea-bundle/scripts/setup.mjs` 时，跑的是建 bundle 那一版的 setup，而不是你刚装的这一版。
  从 **2.0.9** 起，shim 与 setup 都会剥掉 `mirror.json` / `bundle.json` 的 UTF-8 BOM（此前 setup 侧把带 BOM
  的记录读成「没有记录」，会把上一版 manifest 再镜一遍）。**从插件目录**跑一次 `node scripts/setup.mjs`，
  这份镜像副本也会一起刷新。
- **从 `2.0.0-bundle.1` 升级**：那一版镜像了 shim 与 `setup.mjs`，却漏了 manifest，也没有留下插件 checkout
  的记录，所以它供给出来的 bundle **无法自愈** —— 后台供给会因缺 manifest 而崩溃且完全不可见，而它自己写下的
  lock 又会让重试被抑制六小时。请**从插件目录**重跑一次 `node scripts/setup.mjs`：它会重新镜像三个文件，
  并写下让后续运行找到真源的记录。`check-updates.ps1` 会报告这个状态。
- **供给的组件**：重跑 `node scripts/setup.mjs`，它会重新校验盘上的东西，只补缺失或不对的。
  版本钉在 `manifest/bundle.manifest.json`。
- **上游 REA / Ghidra**：改清单里的钉子再重跑 setup。REA 对 Ghidra 有版本闸门（目前 12.1.x），
  所以先更新 REA。

`check-updates.ps1`（Windows PowerShell）会一次性报告以上各项的状态。`npm run check-updates` 在 Windows
上转发给它（优先 PowerShell 5.1，其次 `pwsh`）；在 macOS/Linux 上它会说明这个脚本为何在那里给不出答案，
并列出两条可移植命令 —— `node bin/rea-shim.mjs --shim-status` 与 `node scripts/setup.mjs --dry-run` ——
且以非零码退出，不会报一个自己没查出来的「全绿」。

readme.section: 还想用纯配置的 1.x 线？
readme.text:
1.x 是**不带供给**的适配器：一行配置，从 PATH 上启动 `rea mcp`，并假设 Ghidra 由你自己装好。这些情况它是更合适的选择 ——
你已经自己管理 REA 与 Ghidra、不希望插件去下载任何东西、或者想让那一行继续指向你自己的 `rea`：

```
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-plugin-rea@1.0.6

readme.section: 或钉住分支而不是版本号：
readme.text:
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add github:czcdr/dsh-plugin-rea#v1.0.6
```

两条线发布的 patch 形态与 `mcp__rea__*` 工具面完全相同。1.x 维护在
[`v1` 分支](https://github.com/czcdr/dsh-plugin-rea/tree/v1)，它自己的安装说明也在那里（Node 满足 REA engines、
`npm i -g rea-agents`、原生分析需要 Ghidra 12.1.x）。
